hook_text: A 5 000 litre tank with 3 245 litres inside. One wrong sign and you will try to pour in 8 245 litres.
clip_script: Water tank, 5 000 litres when full, 3 245 inside. How much more fills it? Read it, picture it. The tank is filling up to the top, so the gap is what we want: 5 000 minus 3 245 equals box. Not plus. Plus gives 8 245, and the tank would burst. Calculate: 4 999 minus 3 245 is 1 754, add the 1 back, 1 755 litres. Check the other way: 3 245 plus 1 755 is 5 000. Now the tuck shop: R2 375 Monday, R1 860 Tuesday. Altogether? Add: R4 235. How much more on Monday? Take away: R515. Same numbers, two questions, two signs. Write the unit. Reread the question. And always ask: could a real tank, a real shop, a real runner believe this answer? If not, it is wrong.
visual_style: Whiteboard tank filling to a line with the gap highlighted; a till with two days of takings; a marathon route with a water point marker.
mood: Practical, down to earth, a bit of humour at the bursting tank.
pacing: The tank problem with the wrong-sign warning, the quick calculation and check, then the tuck shop and the story test.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and solve one money problem and one measuring problem from your own day.
